arml-1998-individual-01.prompt:
Numbers are to be placed in the nine squares of a $3\times3$ grid so that the sums of the elements of each row and of each column are equal. If $1$, $9$, $9$, and $8$ are placed as shown, with the unknown entries $X$, $Y$, $Z$ marked, compute $X+Y-Z$.

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline 1&Y&9\\\hline 9&X&Z\\\hline \ &\ &8\\\hline\end{array}$$

arml-1998-individual-02.prompt: Coefficients $a$, $b$, and $c$ of $ax^2+bx+c=0$ are selected without replacement from $N=\{-4,-3,-2,-1,1,2,3,4\}$. Compute the probability that $x=1$ is a solution of the equation.

arml-1998-individual-03.prompt: If the sum of the positive three-digit base ten numbers $\overline{ABC}$, $\overline{CAB}$, and $\overline{BCA}$ can be factored into four distinct primes, compute the largest possible value of the product $A\cdot B\cdot C$.

arml-1998-individual-04.prompt: The sides of a non-right isosceles $\triangle ABC$ are $\sin x$, $\cos x$, and $\tan x$. Compute $\sin x$.

arml-1998-individual-06.prompt: Let $x_n$ be the remainder when $x$ is divided by $n$. For positive integral $x$, compute the sum of all elements in the solution set of $$x^5\left(x_5\right)^5-x^6-\left(x_5\right)^6+x\left(x_5\right)=0.$$

arml-1998-individual-07.prompt: Compute the smallest number $d$ such that fewer than half of the positive integers with $d$ digits have all distinct digits.

arml-1998-individual-08.prompt: In concave hexagon $ABCDEF$, $m\angle A=m\angle B=m\angle C=90^\circ$, $m\angle D=100^\circ$, and $m\angle F=80^\circ$. Also, $CD=FA$, $AB=7$, $BC=10$, and $EF+DE=12$. Compute the area of the hexagon.

arml-1998-individual-tb1.prompt: Let circles $O$ and $Q$ have a common chord $\overline{PS}$. The line of centres $OQ$ meets the chord at $N$, meets circle $Q$ at $M$ and circle $O$ at $T$ (so $M$ and $T$ lie on the segment $OQ$, as in the figure). If $OQ=324$ and $MN:NT=2:1$, compute $OP-PQ$.
